control.scope: one chosen-witness finite instance set: the original 2003 Lemma 3 chain with the derived beta and delta edges replaced by their primitive expansions

derived_control.kind: derived premises (Conditions beta and delta), not primitive source instances
derived_control.label: separately labeled derived control: the published beta/delta proof

fidelity_notes: The exact Egalitarian Dominance and both Dominance Addition statements quantify over equal-sized populations without a positive-size condition, so requiring nonempty A, B and C is the ladder encoding's convention, which only drops instances, not the text's.

Condition beta's displayed statement quantifies over any D, but the Lemma 1.1 and Lemma 1.2 proofs assemble only E inside R(y, x) and R(z, y+1) respectively; the paper's own Lemma 3 applies beta with the negative D2, which only the displayed statement licenses. This is the same boundary that ranged Non-Elitism cannot cross.

The control's numbers are chosen-witness consequences, not source-forced values: four GNEP applications with n_i = 1 give delta's n = 4 at z = -1, m = 1, and the greedy m_i = f(m_{i-1}) = 5, 10, 20 give 35 Non-Elitism applications with m = 35 > 5 = n.
Lemma 1.2's strictness assertion needs r >= 2, since the stated inequalities allow equality at r = 1; the control uses r = 3.

arrhenius-2003:condition-beta.background: any D in the 2003 statement; the proofs assemble only narrower backgrounds (Lemma 1.1 uses E subset R(y, x), Lemma 1.2 uses E subset R(z, y+1)) although D was introduced as any population, so the displayed condition governs the instance and only the proof text is narrower
arrhenius-2003:condition-beta.chain: derived: Non-Elitism implies alpha (Lemma 1.1: n applications of Non-Elitism with each C_i of size p+1 and each B_i of size p give alpha with m = n*p, where p is the Non-Elitism witness), and alpha implies beta (Lemma 1.2: r = x - y applications of alpha with m_i >= f(m_{i-1}) and f(m_i) = m_0+...+m_i, so m = m_1+...+m_r > m_0 = n)
arrhenius-2003:condition-beta.emptiness: D may be empty; m > n forces B nonempty
arrhenius-2003:condition-beta.note: Lemma 1.2's strictness claim needs r >= 2, which holds in Lemma 3 where beta is applied at levels W_{x+2} > W_3 > W_1; the source's own Lemma 3 applies beta with D2 at the negative VRC level, outside Lemma 1.2's R(1, 4) for that application, so the negative-background instance rests on the displayed condition, which is exactly the gap ranged Non-Elitism cannot fill
arrhenius-2003:condition-beta.quantifiers: forall W_x forall W_y forall W_z (x > y > z) forall n>0 exists m>n forall A subset W_x (N=n) forall B subset W_z (N=m) forall C subset W_y (N=m+n) forall D

arrhenius-2003:condition-delta.chain: derived: GNEP implies chi (thesis Lemma 5.2.1 with r = 3 - z applications of GNEP at W_{z+(i-1)}, i = 1..r, and chi's n = n_1+...+n_r), and chi implies delta (thesis Lemma 5.2.2 with m copies of chi, so delta's n = m * n_chi)
arrhenius-2003:condition-delta.emptiness: E may be empty (unstated); the other populations are nonempty by size
arrhenius-2003:condition-delta.levels: W_u, R(1, y) positive with u > y; D at the fixed level W_3
arrhenius-2003:condition-delta.note: the 2003 paper defers this proof to thesis Lemma 5.2 or 2001 Lemma 2
arrhenius-2003:condition-delta.quantifiers: forall W_z (z<0) forall m>0 exists W_u (positive) exists R(1, y) (positive, u > y) exists n>0 forall x >= u forall A subset W_x forall B subset R(1, y) (N=n) forall C subset W_z (N=m) forall D subset W_3 (N=m) forall E

arrhenius-2003:dominance-addition.background: none: C is the addition, not a shared background
arrhenius-2003:dominance-addition.emptiness: the source states only N(A)=N(B), which does not exclude 0; the ladder encoding drops the empty cases and requires C nonempty at one level (the source's 'any number of lives' is silent about zero)
arrhenius-2003:dominance-addition.levels: W_x any level; C must be positive (C subset R(1, Omega))
arrhenius-2003:dominance-addition.note: weak shape W: B union C is at least as good as A; mixed positive C allowed, and applicability is an existence question over splits of B union C
arrhenius-2003:dominance-addition.quantifiers: forall A forall B forall C forall W_x :: A subset R(Omega, x-1), B subset R(x, Omega), N(A)=N(B), C subset R(1, Omega)

arrhenius-2003:egalitarian-dominance.background: none: the condition compares two populations with no shared term
arrhenius-2003:egalitarian-dominance.emptiness: A and B must be nonempty (with A = B = empty the condition would assert empty is better than empty); the text does not say so
arrhenius-2003:egalitarian-dominance.levels: W_x ranges over every indexed level, positive, neutral or negative
arrhenius-2003:egalitarian-dominance.note: strict shape S; the ladder generator emits empty backgrounds only
arrhenius-2003:egalitarian-dominance.quantifiers: forall A forall B (N(A)=N(B)) forall W_x :: B subset R(Omega, x-1) and A subset W_x

arrhenius-2003:general-non-extreme-prior.emptiness: A, B nonempty (n>0); C, D one life each; E may be empty (unstated)
arrhenius-2003:general-non-extreme-prior.levels: W_z any level including the neutral W_0, so the ladder needs W_0; u > y >= 3 because a range has at least three levels
arrhenius-2003:general-non-extreme-prior.note: weak shape W: A union C union E is at least as good as B union D union E
arrhenius-2003:general-non-extreme-prior.quantifiers: forall W_z exists W_u (positive) exists R(1, y) (positive, u > y) exists n>0 forall x >= u forall A subset W_x forall B subset R(1, y) (N=n) forall C subset W_z forall D subset W_{z+1} (N=1) forall E

arrhenius-2003:non-elitism.emptiness: A, B, C nonempty by their sizes; D may be empty (unstated)
arrhenius-2003:non-elitism.levels: no sign restriction; W_{x-1} is the level just below W_x
arrhenius-2003:non-elitism.note: weak shape W: C union D is at least as good as A union B union D
arrhenius-2003:non-elitism.quantifiers: forall W_x forall W_y (x-1 > y) exists n>0 forall A subset W_x (N=1) forall B subset W_y (N=n) forall C subset W_{x-1} (N=n+1) forall D

arrhenius-2003:theorem.chain: Lemma 1 (NE => beta), Lemma 2 (GNEP => delta), Lemma 3 (ED, VRC, DA, beta, delta are inconsistent)
arrhenius-2003:theorem.levels: the proof uses Discreteness, the W_i indexing and unrestricted population sizes as background assumptions
arrhenius-2003:theorem.note: the frozen P8 core is the derived end-point pattern, not a primitive expansion
arrhenius-2003:theorem.quantifiers: no population axiology (reflexive, transitive, not necessarily complete ordering) satisfies (1*)-(5*)

arrhenius-2003:vrc-avoidance.emptiness: A and C nonempty (n, m > 0); B's size is unrestricted and may be empty
arrhenius-2003:vrc-avoidance.levels: W_x negative; A at any single level z >= u (the upper bound v is unused); B in R(1, y)
arrhenius-2003:vrc-avoidance.note: weak shape W: A is at least as good as B union C; this is the source's closing link in Lemma 3
arrhenius-2003:vrc-avoidance.quantifiers: exists W_x (x<0) exists R(u, v) exists R(1, y) (positive, u > y) exists n>0 exists m>0 forall A subset W_z (z >= u, N=n) forall B subset R(1, y) forall C subset W_x (N=m)

thesis:dominance-addition.emptiness: the source states only N(A)=N(B) and leaves N(C) unconstrained; the ladder encoding drops the empty cases and requires C nonempty at one positive level
thesis:dominance-addition.levels: W_x any level; W_y positive, C perfectly equal at W_y
thesis:dominance-addition.note: not-strict shape N: not(A better than B union C); C must be a single positive level, so a mixed positive addition is not an instance; no reverse weak edge without completeness
thesis:dominance-addition.quantifiers: forall A forall B forall C forall W_x forall W_y (y > 0) :: every A life below W_x, every B life at or above W_x, N(A)=N(B), C subset W_y

thesis:non-elitism.background: D subset R(y, x): a ranged background, so no life below W_y
thesis:non-elitism.emptiness: D may be empty (the Condition beta note treats D = empty as admissible)
thesis:non-elitism.note: the 2003 reading has the same body with any D; this is Q-011's ranged weakening and it is what loses the derived beta edge's negative background
thesis:non-elitism.quantifiers: forall W_x forall W_y (x-1 > y) exists n>0 forall A subset W_x (N=1) forall B subset W_y (N=n) forall C subset W_{x-1} (N=n+1) forall D subset R(y, x)
